Listen to this article Share The Oyo State Primary Health Care Board (OYSPHCB) has commenced a nine-day Training of Trainers (ToT) and Facilitating Skills Course on Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) to improve healthcare workers’ capacity to manage common childhood illnesses and reduce preventable deaths among children across the state. Advertisement Advertisement The training, holding at Plaza De Aruna Hotel, Eleekara, Oyo, is aimed at equipping healthcare workers with the knowledge and practical skills needed to promptly identify childhood illnesses, provide appropriate treatment and ensure proper referral of children requiring specialised care. Speaking at the opening ceremony, Maiden Olatunji, Executive Secretary of the Board, represented by the Director of Disease Control and Immunisation, Festus Mustapha, reaffirmed the Board’s commitment to improving child health and strengthening healthcare delivery at the primary level. Read also: Why we are building Nigeria’s healthcare economy He stressed that healthcare workers must be well equipped to recognise early signs of illness in children and respond appropriately, noting that timely diagnosis and treatment could prevent complications and save lives. He explained that the Integrated Management of Childhood Illness strategy provides a comprehensive approach to managing common childhood conditions, adding that its effective implementation would help improve the quality of care children receive at health facilities across the state. Advertisement He urged participants to be attentive, actively engage in the training and make good use of the opportunity to strengthen their professional skills, noting that the success of the programme would depend largely on how well the knowledge acquired is applied in their daily practice. Adepeju Mosunmade, the State Integrated Management of Childhood Illness Programme Officer, emphasised the importance of adhering to IMCI guidelines in assessing and managing sick children, noting that proper assessment, accurate classification and appropriate treatment are crucial to preventing complications and childhood deaths. Advertisement Read also: Candidates lock horns over Lagos budget, healthcare record She highlighted the need for healthcare workers to pay close attention to danger signs in children, communicate effectively with caregivers, maintain proper records and ensure the rational use of medicines, while providing care that is compassionate, timely and evidence-based. Advertisement Advertisement Mosunmade also underscored the importance of the Training of Trainers component, explaining that participants are expected to pass on the knowledge and skills acquired to other healthcare workers, thereby extending the impact of the training to more health facilities and communities. The nine-day course features a combination of classroom sessions, practical demonstrations, case studies, group exercises, clinical simulations and facilitation techniques to ensure participants gain both the clinical knowledge and teaching skills required to effectively implement and train others on IMCI. The training covers the management of common childhood illnesses, including malaria, pneumonia, diarrhoea and malnutrition, with emphasis on early recognition, appropriate treatment, caregiver counselling, follow-up and referral in line with established guidelines. Read also: Lagos governorship candidates outline healthcare reforms at BusinessDay Townhall At the end of the programme, participants are expected to be better equipped to manage childhood illnesses, deliver quality care and train other healthcare workers on the effective implementation of the IMCI strategy at their respective facilities. The Oyo State Primary Health Care Board reiterated its commitment to continuous capacity building of healthcare workers, describing it as a vital step towards strengthening primary healthcare services and improving health outcomes for children across the state. The initiative reflects the Board’s ongoing efforts to reduce preventable childhood deaths, improve access to quality healthcare and ensure that every child receives timely and appropriate medical attention, regardless of location.
